# Widget Gauntlet and Interaction Message Catalog

Yantra's browser-interaction quality gate checks generic widget behavior at both
the protocol-driver seam and the real agent-tool seam. A companion message
catalog keeps model-visible interaction advice complete, distinct, and tied to
capabilities Yantra can actually execute.

The synthetic form layout matrix also checks that every declared control can
be addressed by label, returned as an explicit ambiguity, or used by ref when
there is no label evidence.

This is a maintainer and integrator feature. It adds no CLI command and does not
change any stable interaction error code.

## What It Does

### Runs a 19-fixture protocol gauntlet

The fast tier runs 19 generic HTML fixtures through the production `fillField`
engine with a JSDOM-backed `WidgetPort`. Each registry entry becomes its own
named test case and declares its semantic result and exact operation counts.

| Generic pattern                                                              | Verified result                                                                            | Mutations | Reads |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------: | ----: |
| Undeclared typeahead opens after 300 ms                                      | Commits `Blue offered` after the short probe discovers its popup                           |         2 |    23 |
| `aria-haspopup="true"` input opens after 1.5 s                               | Commits `Blue offered` through the full suggestion watch                                   |         2 |    27 |
| Native datalist accepts free text                                            | Commits `Blue` without a DOM suggestion wait                                               |         1 |     9 |
| Input drops its initial keystroke                                            | Commits `DFW`                                                                              |         3 |    10 |
| Typeahead maps a code to a display label                                     | Commits `Dallas` as a single offered match                                                 |         2 |    17 |
| Picker mounts a duplicate trigger                                            | Commits `San Jose, CA, United States`                                                      |         2 |    17 |
| Read-only date trigger opens a distant month                                 | Commits `Dec 2, 2026` through the calendar driver                                          |         6 |    32 |
| Suggestions arrive after typing settles                                      | Commits `Reykjavik, Iceland`                                                               |         2 |    31 |
| Two suggestions match equally                                                | Refuses ambiguously, then the required follow-up commits                                   |         4 |    29 |
| Trigger routes typing to a detached overlay                                  | Commits the airport label and reports the actual editee                                    |         3 |    22 |
| Suggestions accept only a query prefix                                       | Commits the selected offered value                                                         |         4 |    75 |
| Calendar appears only after an open probe                                    | Commits `Dec 2, 2026` through the calendar driver                                          |         6 |    40 |
| Input rewrites text into a display mask                                      | Commits `(555) 123-4567` as reformatted                                                    |         1 |     9 |
| One date range is split across two inputs                                    | Refuses the incomplete half without changing either input, then the follow-up commits both |         4 |    40 |
| Two range triggers share one calendar                                        | Commits both dates after opening the range once                                            |         4 |    39 |
| Listbox mounts only its in-viewport rows                                     | Commits `Region 6` through the listbox driver                                              |         4 |    18 |
| a calendar with model-identical choices that remain structurally ordered     | Commits `Sep 6, 2026` by stable document order and discloses the structural substitution   |         1 |    16 |
| an option container that mixes genuine choices with paging and mode chrome   | Commits `Economy` while excluding paging, mode-switching, and protected-action controls    |         1 |    12 |
| a calendar ambiguity whose offered label routes back to its originating cell | Refuses with distinct offered labels, then the required follow-up commits `Sep 6, 2026`    |         1 |    18 |

For an engineered refusal, the totals include both the refusal and its mandatory
follow-up. A refusal is accepted only when its `(code, cause)` has a catalog
entry and the follow-up described by its hint reaches a commit. Known
unsupported behavior cannot be registered as a passing terminal result.

The text plan bounds its initial popup probe at 325 ms, with reaction reads at
0, 150, and 300 ms. An observed popup escalates to the full watch; declared
suggestion controls retain that watch from the start. The
`undeclared-haspopup.html` fixture declares `aria-haspopup="true"` despite its
filename. Native datalist suggestions live in Chrome's UI rather than the DOM,
so the datalist fixture verifies the typed free text. These cases preserve the
four-second settling policy where a DOM suggestion watch applies.

The port accounting policy is exhaustive at the TypeScript boundary:

- `click`, `fill`, `clear`, `type`, `press`, and `scrollContainer` are
  mutations;
- `observe`, `evaluate`, and `evaluateOn` are reads; and
- `now` is neutral.

Scrolling a container counts as a mutation because it is page work like any
keystroke: a virtualized list mounts rows in response to it, so a read-classed
scroll would let a driver reveal an unbounded number of options for free.

Every call also appears in a per-method `byAction` breakdown. Adding a
`WidgetPort` method without classifying it fails type checking, while an extra
recovery action or diagnostic read changes a fixture's pinned total and fails
its test.

### Owns the accounting the engine reports

The counting port is the single authority on what actually reached the page.
The fill engine keeps its own tally on the run state it creates per call, and a
seam assertion pins the two together: for a whole `fillField` call — dismissal
and settle work included — the run state's `chargedActions` equals the counting
port's `counts.mutations` and its `chargedReads` equals `counts.reads`. The
committed outcome's reported `actions` total is checked against the same
number. The assertion lives in
`packages/core/tests/fill/fill-engine.spec.ts`, under `one run state per fill
call`.

Because the port is the authority, an attribution change inside the engine —
which rung or sub-plan a charge is booked against, and how the ledger reports
it — must leave every fixture's `expectedMutations` and `expectedReads`
unchanged. The pinned per-fixture totals above are exactly that proof.

### Answers every engineered refusal within four seconds

Each engineered-refusal fixture is also run under a mocked system clock
(`vi.useFakeTimers()` with `vi.runAllTimersAsync()`), and the elapsed injected
time for every one of them must be at most four seconds. The measurement is the
sum of the waits the engine actually chose to take, never wall time, so the
gate is deterministic on the macOS, Windows, and Ubuntu no-LLM matrix instead
of sensitive to machine load.

### Resolves every fixture path from the module URL

Fixture and artifact paths across the test tree are derived from
`dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`, never from the process working
directory, and `packages/core/tests/boundary-rules.spec.ts` carries a rule that
enforces it: any file under `packages/*/tests/**` that reintroduces a
`process.cwd()`-derived path fails the boundary suite.

The rule exists because the two ways of running a subset disagree about the
working directory. `cd packages/core && npx vitest run <path>` leaves the
package as the working directory, while `npx vitest run --root packages/core
<path>` leaves it at the repository root. A cwd-derived fixture path therefore
fails from the repository root with a misleading `ENOENT` that reads like a
real regression rather than a path bug.

### Exercises the wrapped tool in real Chrome

The real-browser tier serves four generic fixtures over loopback, launches
system Chrome, and drives the production wrapped tools through Yantra's normal
middleware and a real `AgentBrowserController`. Two fixtures are filled through
`browser_fill_element`: a search form that replaces its input while text is
entered, and a native select the page encapsulates inside a component's open
shadow tree. The other two are clicked through `browser_click` against a
control something else owns. Every descriptor pins exact controller mutation,
read, top-level tool-call, and engine-initiated clearance totals.

The re-mounting case verifies one top-level tool call, three controller
mutations, and eight controller reads. The form replaces its input while text is
entered, forcing the engine to reacquire the element without asking the model
for another turn. The case parses the model-visible payload, checks that
`winter coat` was committed, resolves every ref in the returned observation,
and confirms that the pre-remount ref now fails with `STALE_ELEMENT_REF`. That
post-action staleness assertion runs only for a fixture that declares a
`remountSelector`, because the contract says something only about a pattern
that remounts its controls.

The shadow-tree case commits `Express` in one controller mutation and six
reads: once the composed tree is walked, an encapsulated native select costs
exactly what a light-DOM one costs. A dedicated case fills the same control by
its accessible name, confirms on the page itself that the commit landed inside
the shadow tree, and asserts that the traversal's internal fields
(`composedScope`, `elementIndex`, `rootNodeDepth`, `selectorIndex`) never reach
the model payload. The fixture's second host holds a _closed_ root with a
structurally identical control, and the same case asserts that control's name
appears nowhere in the observation.

This tier is `@no-llm` and is not skipped by an environment gate. The combined
23-fixture gate is vision-disabled: every descriptor declares that it does not
require vision, the real-browser services run with vision unavailable, and the
wrapped tool catalog must not contain `browser_screenshot`. Chrome discovery
remains environment-dependent, as it is for Yantra's other real-browser tests.

### Enforces choice integrity across the gate

The gate makes the choice contract executable rather than relying on message
wording alone:

- every `offered` array has pairwise-distinct labels after normalization;
- a fixture's declared paging, mode, or protected-action names may not appear
  anywhere in its result;
- every capability-bearing interaction template resolves a concrete receiver
  for every family declared as an emitter; and
- every structurally substituted outcome carries both a model-visible note and
  an attempt-ledger detail. A substitution is permitted only for choices that
  are indistinguishable to the model inside the resolved container; otherwise
  the choice remains an ambiguity for the caller.

### Keeps fixture coverage structural and generic

Both fixture directories are compared with their registries in both
directions. An unregistered HTML file or a registry entry with no file fails
the census, and generic pattern names must be unique.

The protocol tier is additionally pinned at 19 as a literal number, in
`widget-regressions.spec.ts` (against the fixture directory listing) and in
`recovery-characterization.spec.ts` (against `PROTOCOL_GAUNTLET`, together with
its distinct pattern names and its vision-free declaration). With the agent
tier's four, pinned the same way in `widget-gauntlet.spec.ts`, that is the
23-fixture gate. Growing the gallery is therefore a deliberate edit in more
than one place.

Fixtures describe structural widget shapes rather than websites. If a fixture
records a site token as provenance, that token is permitted only inside the
file's leading HTML comment and must not occur in the fixture body or anywhere
under the core or agent production-source trees. Current fixtures otherwise
record generic patterns and, where relevant, originating run IDs.

### Gates field identity across 14 synthetic form layouts

FEAT-055 adds a separate layout matrix in
`packages/test-helpers/src/layout-matrix/`. Its real-Chrome suite,
`packages/core/tests/discovery/layout-matrix.spec.ts`, loads generated HTML
with `setContent` after opening `about:blank`. The pages describe generic DOM
structures and contain no recreated website.

| Fixture               | Ground truth                                                              |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `table-label-cell`    | Two label/control pairs in the same table row                             |
| `stacked-wrappers`    | Label text above the control inside its wrapper                           |
| `css-order-grid`      | Visual order differs from DOM order                                       |
| `floating-labels`     | Label follows the input; placeholder is a space                           |
| `placeholder-only`    | Placeholder and title supply separate fallback labels                     |
| `fieldset-groups`     | Shared legends produce explicit radio/checkbox ambiguity                  |
| `label-after-control` | Wrapper text follows its control                                          |
| `split-controls`      | Individually named phone parts and Month/Day/Year selects                 |
| `describedby-help`    | Help and error text must not become the field label                       |
| `repeated-sections`   | Billing, Shipping, and Office qualify field queries                       |
| `open-shadow`         | Wrapper label inside an open shadow root                                  |
| `dynamic-replacement` | A labelled input and a button that replaces its node                      |
| `over-cap`            | 70 fields with mixed explicit/structural labels plus 30 buttons and links |
| `no-evidence`         | Unbound text supplies no label to either unnamed input                    |

Each `MatrixPage` supplies `id`, `pattern`, `html()`, and `controls`. A
`MatrixControl` supplies its fixture `key`, `role`, and one expectation:

- `{ kind: 'label', query, origin }`: the query must resolve to that exact
  control, and the derived label origin must match. The declared origin type
  is `explicit`, `structural`, `placeholder`, `title`, or `none`.
- `{ kind: 'ambiguous', query, with }`: the query must return ambiguity, with
  exactly the fixture keys in `with` as its offered controls.
- `{ kind: 'ref-only' }`: the field must have origin `none`, and its observed
  ref must resolve to that exact control. Nearby unbound text is never paired
  with unnamed controls by position.

The suite observes at `cap: 400`, maps refs back to fixture keys through their
element handles, and gates all three expectation forms on every page. It also
checks the fixture-key census, including controls inside open shadow roots,
and verifies that ambiguity lists name controls on the same page. Each
observation takes exactly one `evaluateHandle` call for the composed scan.
Fixture keys are test ground truth: a boundary test prohibits `data-fixture-`
in production sources under `packages/*/src`.

`packages/core/tests/discovery/layout-matrix-baseline.json` preserves the
pre-change per-page `resolved`, `ambiguous`, and `unresolvable` counts. Current
coverage is enforced by the expectations rather than by matching those old
counts. The baseline test checks its page IDs and rejects raw control bytes
other than tabs and line endings; ordinary runs leave the file untouched.

### Shares the layout fixtures with later reliability slices

Import `layoutMatrix` and its types from the dedicated
`@yantra/test-helpers/layout-matrix` subpath. This entry imports only fixture
modules and types, so it can be loaded without importing Vitest. The package's
root entry is not required to consume these fixtures.

The reuse contract for FEAT-057 through FEAT-060 is to consume and extend this
same matrix for fill performance, deliverable capture, progress tracking, and
action-evidence scenarios. Keep generic layouts and declared control ground
truth together, preserve the historical baseline, and retain the existing
resolution gate when adding scenario assertions. These reusable fixtures do
not themselves establish live-provider task-completion or timing results.

### Measures fill throughput and continuation on forty controls

FEAT-057 extends the shared fixture package with `fortyControls` and
`fortyControlValue`. This separate page has 40 explicitly labelled physical
controls: ordinary inputs and textareas, four native selects, three checkboxes,
three radio buttons, and a masked phone input. The radio buttons share one
group, so fill progress counts 38 eligible census units. No suggestion
declaration is present, and the submit handler counts accidental submissions.

`packages/core/tests/fill/fill-performance.spec.ts` fills every physical
control through the production engine in real Chrome. It asserts zero full
`watch-and-select` entries, total fill time at most 60 seconds, the first ten
ordinary fields at most 15 seconds, and zero submissions. It also counts
`evaluateOn` calls directly on the controller, so internal calls are visible.
`packages/core/tests/fixtures/fill-performance/baseline.json` stores measured
before/after timings and operation counts as informational context, rather than
requiring future runs to match those measurements. The recorded core total
improves from about 169.7 seconds to 50.9 seconds, with full-watch entries
falling from 30 to zero.

The separate real-Chrome case in `e2e/agent-browser.spec.ts` uses wrapped
`browser_fill_form` calls and follows `progress.next`. Its first batch reports
10 filled of 38 eligible units. One number field deliberately rejects an
invalid value; four batches leave that field outstanding, and a fifth call
corrects it. Final progress is 38 filled, zero remaining, and an empty `next`.
The test verifies every physical control's final value or checked state,
including the mask and one selected radio sibling, and asserts zero submissions.

The continuation assertions distinguish semantic resends from engine retries:
each committed field is sent once and mutated once, while the failed field is
sent twice and may incur additional internal recovery mutations. Tool-call
audit durations must total at most 60 seconds, and the first ordinary ten-field
batch must take at most 15 seconds. The recorded five-call total is 53.873
seconds; the deliberately failing batch is not an ordinary ten-field timing
sample. These fixture measurements do not establish live-provider completion
targets or completion of the feature's remaining verification gates.

### Catalogs model-visible interaction messages

Catalog ownership follows the production package boundary:

- core owns fill failures, browser actionability failures, and fill success
  notes; and
- agent owns registered browser-tool and shared middleware messages, including
  confirmation, budget, timeout, abort, and phase failures.

Each entry is keyed by `(surface, code, cause)` and declares its message, hint,
required detail keys, and optional engine or tool capability. The internal
`cause` chooses wording but is not serialized in fill failures.

Contract tests enforce the following current invariants:

- catalog keys and rendered messages are globally distinct;
- every message renders when supplied with its declared details, while missing
  templates or details fail explicitly;
- engine capabilities resolve to public core functions and tool capabilities
  resolve against the active wrapped-tool catalog;
- interaction-layer error-code literals in the scanned agent sources have a
  core- or agent-owned catalog entry;
- the established core error-code set remains frozen; and
- a budget result that already contains the publication remedy does not receive
  the same sentence a second time.

The catalog changes ownership and verification of existing copy; it does not
rename error codes or expose the internal failure cause.

### Enforces explicit UTF-8 assertions

Fixture and artifact text used by the gauntlet is decoded with a fatal UTF-8
decoder. Invalid CP-1252/Latin-1 byte sequences throw instead of becoming
replacement characters, and every rendered catalog message is verified through
a UTF-8 encode/decode round trip.

On Windows PowerShell 5.1, inspect these files with an explicit decoder, for
example:

```powershell
Get-Content -Encoding utf8 <path>
[System.IO.File]::ReadAllText(<path>)
```

### Gates the recovery-verdict migration

The checked-in legacy fixture preserves the previous shape in which a successful
recovery rung could carry `errorCode: null` inside a later overall failure's
`details.attempted` ledger. The current gate prohibits that nullable success form
at production tool seams: attempted entries are discriminated verdicts, and only
a failed verdict contains `error_code`. Reader tests normalize the legacy fixture
without modifying it or any existing run directory.

The gauntlet's own ledger expectations read that same verdict projection. Each
attempted record carries a `verdict` of `succeeded`, `failed`, or `skipped`, so
an assertion about which drivers were tried filters the `skipped` entries out
before comparing strategies, and a measured field a rung never recorded is
omitted rather than emitted as a zero.

## How to Use It

Run a focused tier from its own workspace directory. The working directory is
part of the command, because fixture paths resolve from the test module and the
runner is invoked directly:

```bash
cd packages/core && npx vitest run tests/interaction/widget-regressions.spec.ts tests/interaction/message-catalog.spec.ts
cd packages/core && npx vitest run tests/interaction/recovery-characterization.spec.ts tests/fill/fill-engine.spec.ts tests/boundary-rules.spec.ts
cd packages/agent && npx vitest run tests/runtime/message-catalog.spec.ts
cd e2e && npx vitest run widget-gauntlet.spec.ts
```

For the synthetic layout matrix, first build its shared fixtures from the
repository root, then run the real-browser gate from the core workspace:

```bash
pnpm --filter @yantra/test-helpers build
cd packages/core && npx vitest run tests/discovery/layout-matrix.spec.ts tests/boundary-rules.spec.ts
```

Leave `UPDATE_LAYOUT_BASELINE` unset for normal verification. Setting it to
`1` rewrites the baseline with current counts; it does not recreate the
historical pre-change measurement.

For fill performance, build shared fixtures and core before running the
separate core and wrapped-tool scenarios:

```bash
pnpm --filter @yantra/test-helpers build
npx turbo run build --filter=@yantra/core
cd packages/core && npx vitest run tests/fill/fill-performance.spec.ts
cd e2e && npx vitest run agent-browser.spec.ts -t 'continues a forty-control form'
```

Run each `cd` command from the repository root. Leave `UPDATE_FILL_AFTER`
unset for ordinary checks; setting it to `1` updates the informational `after`
measurement while retaining the historical baseline. The e2e workspace uses
built core output, so rebuild after changing core behavior.

`pnpm --filter <pkg> test -- <pattern>` is not a way to run a subset: the
pattern is silently ignored and the whole package suite runs. Use the
`cd <workspace> && npx vitest run <path>` form above instead.

Run the complete model-free gate across workspaces from the repository root
with:

```bash
pnpm test:no-llm
```

When adding a protocol fixture, add its HTML file and one
`PROTOCOL_GAUNTLET` descriptor. Give it a unique generic-pattern description,
an exact outcome, and pinned mutation/read totals. An engineered refusal must
also declare a cataloged failure and a follow-up that commits, and must still
answer within four seconds of the injected clock. Because the tier size is
pinned as a literal, also update the census numbers in
`widget-regressions.spec.ts`, `recovery-characterization.spec.ts`, and the
combined gate in `widget-gauntlet.spec.ts`.

When a test needs to read a fixture or artifact from disk, resolve its path
from `dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`. A `process.cwd()`-derived path
anywhere under a package's `tests/` fails the boundary suite.

When adding a real-browser fixture, add its HTML file and one `AGENT_GAUNTLET`
descriptor with exact mutation, read, and top-level tool-call totals. When
adding model-visible interaction copy, register its surface, code, cause,
required details, and any capability rather than introducing an untracked
inline message.

## Inputs and Outputs

The gate has no runtime CLI input. Its test registries consume fixture
descriptors containing identity, generic pattern, field intent, expected
outcome, provenance, and operation budgets.

Protocol execution produces an in-memory per-fixture result with:

- fixture file, pattern, and tier;
- `commit`, `engineered-refusal`, or `failed` outcome;
- mutation, read, and top-level tool-call totals; and
- a `byAction` per-method breakdown.

The test runner is the gallery's reporting surface. The gallery does not create
a new durable artifact. The real-browser tier checks the wrapped tool's existing
status, error code, and JSON `modelText` payload, but it does not recreate the
orchestrator-owned `tool-calls.jsonl` projection.

The layout matrix consumes generated HTML and control expectations. Its
per-page counts stay in memory during ordinary runs, and its checked-in
baseline remains a historical input.

The fill-performance scenarios retain a checked-in informational timing
baseline. The continuation case writes temporary `tool-calls.jsonl` end records
to sum tool durations and inspect existing result details; this scripted harness
does not run the agent orchestrator.

Catalog rendering returns existing model-visible message and hint text. Missing
catalog entries or required detail values throw a typed dangling-message error
instead of falling back to generic advice.

## Configuration and Permissions

The protocol and catalog tiers need no credentials, model provider, network
access, or feature-specific configuration. The real-browser tier requires a
discoverable compatible system Chrome, opens only the local fixture server,
and uses temporary run/profile state that is removed during teardown.

No fixture performs a secret fill, and all three tiers are tagged `@no-llm`.

The layout matrix is also tagged `@no-llm` and requires a compatible system
Chrome. It uses isolated temporary browser state and offline DOM fixtures.

## Limitations

- The current gallery contains 23 fixtures: 19 protocol cases and four
  real-browser wrapped-tool cases (a re-mounting search form, an open
  shadow-root native select, a page-blocking consent modal, and a
  viewport-pinned band that owns a control's click point). Both halves are
  pinned as numbers, so growing the gallery is a deliberate edit.
- The original 14-page layout matrix is a separate gate from that 23-fixture gallery.
  Its matrix suite verifies field discovery and resolution; it does not click
  the dynamic-replacement button. The additional `forty-controls` fixture has
  separate fill-performance and wrapped-tool continuation checks.
- An undeclared popup that first appears after the 325 ms probe window may be
  missed. Declared suggestion controls retain the full watch. Native datalist
  option selection is not exercised; the datalist case verifies free text.
- Real-Chrome timing gates depend on machine load. The checked-in measurements
  describe one run; ordinary batches have a 15-second gate and the deliberately
  failing batch can take longer. These checks do not measure model latency or
  prove autonomous task completion.
- A control inside a _closed_ shadow root is out of scope and is never counted
  as a pass. The platform returns `null` for `host.shadowRoot` on a closed
  root, and no piercing library and no DOM tagging is used to get around that,
  so such a control is absent from the observation rather than filtered out of
  it. The closed-root half of the open-shadow fixture is asserted as absent and
  contributes no gallery entry.
- The real-browser harness validates the wrapped result but has no run
  orchestrator, so durable tool-call audit projection remains covered by the
  run-recorder suite.
- Exact counts intentionally make implementation-cost changes visible. A
  legitimate engine change may require a reviewed registry count update even
  when the semantic outcome is unchanged.
- The legacy successful-rung `errorCode: null` fixture remains intentionally
  checked in to prove old artifacts normalize; current tool output may not emit
  that shape.
